Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopNova Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for those wishing to ask a question will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopNova Inc.'s Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Emily Carter, CEO; Michael Reyes, CFO; Lisa Nguyen, COO; David Patel, CMO; Rachel Kim, CTO; Kevin Lopez, CDO; and Sophia Grant, CSO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Emily Carter, CEO of ShopNova Inc.

Emily Carter:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by robust GMV growth and efficient customer acquisition strategies that lowered our CAC while boosting active buyer counts. We saw significant growth in key metrics, with GMV up 17% year-over-year to $28.4 billion and revenue climbing 15% to $7.2 billion.

Our focus remains on optimizing promotional activities to drive sales without sacrificing profitability, even as we navigate macroeconomic headwinds like inflation and interest rates. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our AI-powered personalization tools, which we believe will significantly enhance conversion rates and repeat purchases.

We are investing heavily in supply chain efficiencies and technology infrastructure to manage operating expenses tightly.

We are focused on improving advertising efficiency, with ROAS reaching new highs.

We are expanding our presence in high-growth regions like APAC through strategic partnerships.

We are enhancing our customer experience through data-driven retention initiatives.

Finally, we are committed to sustainability efforts that reduce our environmental footprint while aligning with consumer values.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Reyes, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Reyes:
Thank you, Emily. Our Q2 revenue was $7.2 billion, an increase of 15% year-over-year. Gross margin was 32.1%, driven by a mix of private-label expansion and optimized fulfillment, though pressured by deeper promotions. Operating expenses were $5.1 billion, representing 71% of revenue, reflecting strong leverage from our efficiency programs.

Let me dive deeper into the key aspects shaping our results. Starting with Gross Merchandise Value, or GMV, which remains the cornerstone of our marketplace flywheel. For the quarter ended June 30, 2024, we delivered total GMV of $28.4 billion, up 17% year-over-year and 6.2% quarter-over-quarter. This marks a strong beat against our guidance range of 15-18% YoY and 5-7% QoQ growth, underscoring the resilience of our platform amid a softening macro environment characterized by persistent inflation pressures and cautious consumer spending in discretionary categories.

Breaking it down regionally, North America, which accounted for 52% of our Q2 GMV at $14.8 billion, grew 19% YoY and 7.1% QoQ, exceeding our guided 16-19% YoY range. This was fueled by a 25% surge in active buyers, driven by our AI-powered personalization engine—now live for 85% of US traffic—which boosted conversion rates by 12% through hyper-targeted recommendations. We also saw outsized gains in high-margin categories like beauty and wellness, up 28% YoY, thanks to partnerships with DTC brands like Glossier and Fenty Beauty, whose shop-in-shop integrations drove 40% higher repeat purchase rates.

In Europe, representing 28% of GMV at $7.9 billion, we posted 16% YoY growth and 5.8% QoQ, right in line with our 14-17% guidance despite regulatory headwinds from the DSA and DMA. Our localized fulfillment network, expanded with new micro-warehouses in Poland and Spain via a deepened alliance with DHL, reduced delivery times to under 48 hours for 70% of orders—directly contributing to a 15% uplift in cross-border GMV from non-EU sellers. Fashion and apparel grew 22% YoY here, benefiting from live-streaming events that generated $450 million in incremental GMV during peak promotional weeks.

APAC and Emerging Markets delivered 14% YoY and 5.5% QoQ growth on $5.7 billion of GMV—slightly ahead of our 12-15% guide. India and Southeast Asia were standouts, with GMV up 32% YoY, propelled by our QuickCommerce vertical, which crossed $1.2 billion in quarterly run-rate and now serves 15 million MAUs via on-demand partnerships with local players like BigBasket and JioMart. Brazil contributed a solid 18% YoY lift, though we navigated FX volatility; our hedging strategies mitigated a potential 3% headwind.

QoQ dynamics reflected seasonal tailwinds from back-to-school ramp-ups and Father's Day promotions, plus a 10% increase in average order value to $145, driven by upselling via our dynamic bundling algorithms. Take rate expanded 120 basis points to 18.5%, supported by premium seller tools like Sponsored Products, which saw 35% adoption among our top 10,000 merchants.

These results validate our 'Scale with Intelligence' initiative: $250 million invested in FY2024 so far on supply chain automation, including robotic sortation centers that cut fulfillment costs by 18% per unit. We've also accelerated our GenAI roadmap, rolling out demand forecasting tools—reducing stockouts by 22% and enabling just-in-time inventory for 60% of SKUs. Looking ahead, we're guiding Q3 GMV growth to 16-19% YoY.

Turning to active buyer count growth, which powers our flywheel. We define an active buyer as any unique customer who has completed at least one purchase in the trailing 12 months. Q3 active buyer count grew 18% year-over-year to 285 million globally, accelerating from 14% in Q2. This marks our strongest quarterly expansion since Q4 2021, driven by aggressive user acquisition and sticky retention.

We added 42 million net new active buyers, up 25% YoY. CAC held steady at $28 per new buyer despite a 15% ramp-up in paid media spend to $1.2 billion. Paid search and Google Shopping accounted for 35% of new acquisitions at 3.2x ROAS, while social commerce like TikTok Shop exploded 45% YoY. Organically, SEO drove 28% of inflows. APAC led with 32% new buyer growth to 112 million actives; North America grew 12% to 98 million; EMEA surged 22%.

Retention improved to 76% annually, up 300 basis points YoY. Our Prime-like subscription hit 145 million members, delivering 85% retention. Recommendation algorithms lifted cross-sell by 22%; mobile notifications re-engaged 28% of lapsed cohorts. Grocery and essentials now 32% of GMV with 2.2x repeat rates. We guide Q4 growth to 16-19% YoY.

Now, on customer acquisition cost, or CAC, and the efficiency and ROI of our marketing spend. In the hyper-competitive e-commerce landscape—where giants like Amazon, Walmart, and Shopify merchants battle for every click—CAC discipline is a survival imperative amid rising ad costs, iOS privacy changes, and cookie signal loss.

Our blended CAC was $42 per new customer, a 19% improvement YoY from $52, and down 8% sequentially from $46. This came from $168 million in marketing spend—up 12% YoY—yielding 4 million new customers, up 28%. Payback period is 4.2 months on $85 AOV and $520 CLV; LTV-to-CAC is 12.4x, above the 3-5x benchmark.

By channel: Paid Search (42% spend) at 8.2x ROAS, $28 CPA; Social (35%) at 6.5x, $38 CPA; Affiliates (12%) at 10x; Organic (11%) effectively $0. Regionally: NA $39; EMEA $58; APAC $35, with WeChat Mini Program at $22 CPA.

Pillars: Tech modernization with server-side tagging and ML models at 88% CLV accuracy; cohort optimization lifting Day 30 retention 18%; performance shift cutting brand spend 25%. Q3 CAC steady at $40-$44.

Next, the impact of promotional activities on sales and profitability. We executed 14 major campaigns, including 'Summer Flash Fest,' driving 28% YoY GMV to $4.2 billion, with promos at 42% of total. Order volume up 15% to 49 million; AOV steady at $85.

NA up 32%, Europe 22%, APAC 45%. Gross margin down 420 bps to 32.1% from 25% discounts; marketing to 14.2%; EBITDA margin to 8.5%. Mitigated via dynamic pricing on private-label, halo effects boosting LTV 18% to $420.

Evolving with 'Smart Promo 2.0' for personalized offers, NexClub loyalty at 40 million. Q3 GMV growth 25-30%, margins 33-34%.

On seasonality impacts, our business is inherently seasonal, with Q4 averaging 42% of annual revenue historically. Q2 was soft at 21% of annual GMV $3.9 billion, flat YoY due to inflation eroding apparel AOV. Q3 back-to-school beat at 18%, up 15%.

Q4 hit $7.8 billion, 28% YoY. BFCM $2.1 billion up 32%; supply chain resilience stabilized margins at 38.5%. Deviations from macro, regional dynamics mitigated by ML models and micro-events.

Macroeconomic factors weighed on us: Q3 GMV $2.85 billion up 4.2% YoY, missing guide due to 3.2% CPI, 5.25% rates, 4.1% unemployment. Discretionary down 6-8%; essentials up 15%. AOV compressed 5% to $68.

NA 3%, Europe flat, APAC +12%. Countered with AI personalization adding 220 bps GMV, nearshoring cutting costs 12%, Rewards 2.0 lifting LTV 14%.

Operating expenses totaled $5.1 billion, 71% of revenue, down 400 bps YoY. Fulfillment $2.8 billion (39%), down from 43% via AI forecasting, shipping $4.25/unit, returns 18%. Marketing $1.2 billion (17%), CAC $28, ROAS 4.5x. Tech $650 million (9%), GenAI cutting stockouts 40%. G&A down 8%.

Finally, advertising efficiency: Blended ROAS 5.8x, up 18% YoY. Google 6.7x, Meta 5.2x, TikTok 8.1x. Mitigated cookies with first-party data; incrementality 65%. NA 6.2x, EMEA 4.9x, APAC 5.4x. SphereOptix ML lifts CTR 22%. Q3 6.0-6.3x.

Our net income was $500 million, or $1.20 per share. We ended with $3.5 billion in cash. Reaffirming full-year guidance of $30-32 billion revenue, 17-19% EBITDA margins.

Now I'll turn it over to Lisa Nguyen to discuss operations.

Lisa Nguyen:
Thanks, Michael. Operationally, we focused on supply chain automation and micro-fulfillment expansions. Our shipping times improved by 25%. Fulfillment costs were down 18%. We are implementing robotic sortation in new centers.

Now I'll turn it over to David Patel.

David Patel:
Thanks, Lisa. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from Summer Flash Fest and TikTok Shop integrations. Customer acquisition costs were $42. Our brand awareness increased by 20%. We are focusing on social commerce and retail media networks.

Now I'll turn it over to Rachel Kim.

Rachel Kim:
Thanks, David. On the technology front, we've been focused on GenAI personalization and server-side tracking. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 30%. We're investing in cookieless attribution and demand forecasting tools.

Now I'll turn it over to Kevin Lopez.

Kevin Lopez:
Thanks, Rachel. Data science is a key focus. We've seen a 12% improvement in conversion rates because of our NovaAI recommendation suite. We are also focusing on first-party data platforms for privacy compliance.

Now I'll turn it over to Sophia Grant.

Sophia Grant:
Thanks, Kevin. Sustainability is very important to us. We reduced our carbon footprint by 20%. We are committed to electric vehicle fleets in fulfillment and sustainable sourcing for 40% of products.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Jamie Lee with Goldman Sachs.

Jamie Lee:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Michael, can you expand on the CAC improvements and how you're thinking about channel shifts into Q3?

Michael Reyes:
Thanks, Jamie. As I detailed, our CAC drop to $42 was driven by high-ROAS channels like paid search at 8.2x and APAC efficiencies. We're shifting more to bottom-funnel retail media, expecting stability at $40-44 in Q3 despite Black Friday ramps.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Morgan Stanley.

Alex Rivera:
Great, thanks. On promotions, how did the deeper discounts impact profitability, and what's the outlook for holiday margins?

Michael Reyes:
Alex, promos drove 42% of GMV but compressed margins 420 bps. Halo effects and private-label preserved LTV. Holidays should stabilize at 33-34% via co-ops and personalization.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Taylor Chen with JPMorgan.

Taylor Chen:
Thanks. Lisa, operations-wise, how are the new micro-warehouses contributing to shipping improvements amid macro pressures?

Lisa Nguyen:
Taylor, they've cut delivery to under 48 hours for 70% of orders, improving NPS and repeat rates by 15%, offsetting inflation in freight.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Morgan Patel with Barclays.

Morgan Patel:
David, marketing efficiency looks strong—can you talk ROAS by region and TikTok's role?

David Patel:
Morgan, blended 5.8x, TikTok at 8.1x leading APAC gains. NA at 6.2x from Amazon synergies; we're expanding CTV for holidays.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Riley Wong with Citi.

Riley Wong:
Thanks. Rachel, tech investments in GenAI—any quantification on conversion lifts?

Rachel Kim:
Riley, NovaAI boosted conversions 12-18% via real-time recs, with stockout reductions of 22-40%, directly supporting GMV beats.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Casey Ellis with Deutsche Bank.

Casey Ellis:
Kevin, on data initiatives, how is the CDP helping with retention amid seasonality?

Kevin Lopez:
Casey, 95% first-party match rates predict CLV at 88% accuracy, lifting Day 30 retention 18% and smoothing Q2 troughs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jordan Grant with UBS.

Jordan Grant:
Sophia, sustainability—how are carbon reductions tying into ops efficiencies?

Sophia Grant:
Jordan, EV fleets cut fuel 12%, aligning with fulfillment leverage and EU regs, while sustainable sourcing boosts brand loyalty.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Emily Carter for closing remarks.

Emily Carter:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
